explicit_propositions.text: Words, names, and understanding their meanings are very important.
Misusing the name of the Lord leads to confusion and misunderstandings.
The third commandment prohibits misusing the name of the Lord your God.
God will not hold guiltless anyone who misuses His name.
Some ancient Jewish traditions avoided pronouncing or writing the name of the Lord due to reverence.
Using 'Oh my God' casually is considered a misuse of God's name.
A low view of God often leads to careless or disrespectful use of His name.
God is described in Scripture as holy, awesome, eternal, and all-powerful.
God’s omniscience means He knows every detail of creation, including the number of stars and hairs on one’s head.
Communion is a sacred opportunity to repent and reaffirm devotion to God.

assumptions.text: The listener holds religious beliefs consistent with Christianity and values biblical authority.
The speaker's emotional reaction to name misuse reflects genuine spiritual conviction rather than performative piety.
Language shapes worldview and moral perception, especially regarding divine names.
Divine holiness requires proportional reverence in human speech and behavior.
Sinful habits like casual swearing stem from deeper theological distortions, not mere linguistic negligence.
Repentance and confession lead to purification and reconciliation with God.
God possesses emotions and experiences relational hurt when His name is disrespected.
Theological reflection directly influences personal conduct, particularly in speech.
Scripture is the ultimate source of truth about God’s nature and expectations.
Community accountability is both possible and morally required when witnessing profanity involving God's name.
